title: Firmness gate between extraction and ledger, AMI test split, single run

gate.keep_if: log P(YES) - log P(NO) of the first token >= tau
gate.system: You check one entry proposed for a meeting's decision ledger against the meeting transcript.
gate.question:
YES only if the speakers settle it here: they decide, agree, confirm or commit to {value} for {item}.
NO if {value} is only suggested, proposed, preferred, asked about, discussed, hoped for, hypothetical or reported as someone's idea, or if the excerpt is not about {value} for {item}.
Examples from another meeting series (entry: Caterer = Firm P):
"Fine, we go with Firm P." -> YES
"So Firm P it is then. Okay." -> YES
"Should we ask Firm P for a quote?" -> NO
"I think Firm P would be nice." -> NO
"Firm P delivered the lunch late." -> NO
In this excerpt, is {value} for {item} firmly decided or committed, not proposed, discussed or hypothetical?
gate.scorer: src-tauri/resources/memory/qwen_scoring.py first_token_logprobs (YES - NO), app worker via MEMORIA_QWEN_SOCKET

chosen_on_dev.rule: wording: higher dev AUROC (gold-matched vs other events reaching the ledger), context variant; tau: integer grid -8..8 maximising dev QA (ext+router), ties by dev extraction F1, then |tau| smallest
chosen_on_dev.caveat: dev AUROC is near chance for every configuration and the dev QA gain is one grid point wide; a null test result is the expected outcome

test.split: test (ES2004, ES2014, IS1009, TS3003, TS3007): 20 meetings, 96 questions, 46 gold events
test.extraction: October candidates replayed from results/cache (ami_test_memoria.jsonl; review: ami_test_memoria_review.jsonl); a cache miss stops the run
test.primary: QA accuracy, ext+router, 96 questions, gated vs October ledger (59/96); exact two-sided paired sign test
secondary: accuracy per question type (current, as_of_valid, n_changes) vs October 18/34, 29/29, 12/33
extraction precision, recall, F1 vs gold (October 21%, 67%, 32%)
suggestions a reviewer sees per meeting, confirm_conflicts with the perfect reviewer (October 1.75), and the app's confirm_all
perfect-reviewer QA (October 85/96), sign test; accepted proposals the gate removes
test.hypothesis: fewer spurious events, higher current and n_changes accuracy, fewer suggestions, small recall loss
